title: Session identity
summary: Scope is fixed at registration: the registered project it started in, or its authority's organization outside any project; retries, reactivation and folder changes keep it. Authenticated function calls carry the actor session through nested Conduct task-status claim checks. Exact task claims or parent authority authorize the write; payload identity and the server process session do not. Retained local calls use canonical ambient identity. Authorized session rosters, ended history, machine usage, machine pages and boards include owned or org-readable sessions outside any project. An authenticated all-scope public board admits an actor with no readable projects only when it can operate an outside-project session; project data stays hidden. Configured session and timeline scopes cannot expand readable project authority, including numeric selections. Explicit numeric and slug session project refs resolve within caller visibility; unavailable refs return normal not_found or empty mode-specific results. Explicit project filters exclude org sessions. Each session card links its executor label to the registered session detail; outside-project sessions open without a project filter, rather than borrowing the first project. Search input and blur/change notifications with the same filter values do not rebuild session cards, so the first click on a filtered label retains its anchor through activation. Local boards use the universe-proven operating actor and refuse an unavailable identity. These are source behaviors; deployed proof is pending.
